**[#2922](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2922) — value-to-declare pass not handling pointer case under -O1**  
<sub>batch 008 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (model not self-identifiable)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (blind reproducibility check, SKILL.md step "Test reproducibility"; and independent draft review, SKILL.md step 10, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Does not reproduce on main (ab5400907). Fixed between v1.6.2112 and v1.7.2207; the evidence points to c0676c7ca (PR #4375, Apr 2022), which stopped DxilDbgValueToDbgDeclare unconditionally early-returning on pointer-typed llvm.dbg.value. Measured by running each release's own -dxil-dbg-value-to-dbg-declare over PixStructAnnotation_FloatN's shader via dxopt -external: at -O1 the pass emits 0 llvm.dbg.declare on v1.6.2104/2106/2112 and 2 on v1.7.2207 through main. The reporter's own repro now passes 18/18, and the same commit deleted the three "don't run -O1 test until pointer types are dealt with" opt-outs from PixTest.cpp. Attribution is strong but window-bounded and not proven: 248 commits, 3 of them touching the pass, none built in isolation. NOTE: cmd.txt and the bisect line measure only the precondition, not the symptom - dxc.exe cannot run PIX passes.

<sub>batch 002 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

SPIR-V printf heap corruption. A captured repeated-run set reproduced STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xC0000374) in 33/40 v1.6.2104 runs and 28/40 v1.6.2106 runs; v1.5.2010 and v1.6.2112 were each clean in 30/30, and later release probes were clean through v1.9.2607. The v1.9.2607 release binary and current main Debug were each clean in 55/55 runs across ps_6_0 and cs_6_0, with expected SPIR-V inspected on main. The reported retail-heap stack detects the bad free during front-end parsing, before legalization, but does not identify the original write. The original -fcgl -Vd flags avoided a separate SPIRV-Tools crash fixed by PR #4280; all four flag combinations repeatedly reproduce on both affected releases, so the flags do not suppress this crash. **[#8732](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8732) — [SPIR-V] SPV_EXT_descriptor_heap mixed bound/heap aliasing causes silent miscompilation or ICE**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Filed against the unmerged branch of PR #8517; the VarDecl alias map it blames does not exist on main (zero occurrences of descriptorHeapImageAliasVars, createDescriptorHeapIndexVar, diagnoseDescriptorHeapAliasMixing et al). On main at ab5400907 all five cases fail loudly instead of silently: defects 1-3 and the still-undiagnosed heap-only conditional die on 'generated SPIR-V is invalid: [VUID-StandaloneSpirv-OpTypeImage-06924] Cannot store to OpTypeImage', defect 4 on 'UAV support not implemented with non-emulated heaps'. Re-run with -Vd the module is semantically correct -- both descriptors store into one Function image variable, last store wins, %boundTex preserved -- so main is illegal, not wrong; Interlocked* on a heap-loaded texture is simply unsupported there (a heap-only control with no bound resource fails identically). v1.9.2607 matches main exactly. Separately, the reporter's documented workaround (separate variables) compiles on v1.9.2607 but now fails on main with the UniformConstant ArrayStride rule newly enforced by the SPIRV-Tools 1c336172 bump (ec2ba18da), tracked as #8740 -- so every shader here that actually indexes ResourceDescriptorHeap fails validation on main today, though a control that sets -fspv-use-descriptor-heap without indexing the heap still compiles.

**[#3005](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3005) — Generated separate PDB files have possibly invalid header**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79-2 (model not self-identifiable)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Still reproduces on main (ab5400907). The separate PDB written by -Fd declares NumBlocks one block short, so the file's own stream directory addresses a block the superblock says does not exist; cause is NumBlockAddrBlocks being written but never counted at lib/DXIL/DxilPDB.cpp:132. Present in all 21 builds measured. LLVM and llvm-pdbutil accept the file; Microsoft's reference MSF implementation would refuse to read the last page. The actionable finding is that PR #5767 (Fixes #3005, by a maintainer, reviewed and format-clean in Nov 2023) was closed unmerged by an inactivity sweep on 2026-01-22.

**[#3305](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3305) — Empty Payload struct not recognized in DXIL**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-sonnet-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

DXIL still rejects an empty payload struct while SPIR-V compiles it, unchanged on every measurable build (v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 and main). The DXIL diagnostic misnames its cause: it says the shader must include an inout payload structure parameter, but the parameter is present and what CGHLSLMS.cpp:2492 checks is payloadSizeInBytes == 0 -- a payload whose only member is an empty struct gets the same message, and since PR #5131 (2023-04) a genuinely missing parameter gets an accurate Sema message instead. Whether an empty payload should be legal is a language/product decision, deliberate since 2018 and still unanswered on the thread; the wrong message is separately fixable either way.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`.

**[#2128](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2128) — Generated bytecode by dxc has very higher compression ratio**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Confirmed and unchanged since v1.4.1907. dxc objects zip to 3.7x fxc's for the same shaders (fxc ratio 0.33 vs reporter's ~0.30; dxc -Qstrip_reflect 0.77 vs reporter's 0.80-0.85); raw sizes differ by 1.5%, so the whole gap is compressibility. The DXIL part alone deflates to 0.848/0.900 -- LLVM 3.7 bitcode is bit-packed and near entropy-dense where DXBC's SHEX is byte-aligned repetitive tokens (0.271). Half of BitMD's 2019 comment landed: reflection moved out of the module into STAT between v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010, cutting corpus size 39% raw, but the bitcode's compressibility never moved (0.839 -> 0.851 -> 0.848). Division's 2022 question answered: PC dxc has no shader-object compression to disable -- zlib is used only by the PDB writer and the SRCI source part. Not a defect; a container-encoding decision.

*Labels:* add `fxc-disagrees`, `enhancement`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* The symptom is the byte size and deflate ratio of the compiled object. Compiler Explorer panes show text disassembly; no pane can show an object's byte count, and none can run deflate. A link would show fxc, dxc and clang all succeeding, which published bare reads as 'cannot reproduce' -- the #2191 trap, and here without even #2191's partial value (there is no release-vs-debug distinction to demonstrate). A Clang pane was considered and rejected for the same reason: clang's HLSL path emits the same LLVM bitcode encoding, so it inherits the property by construction, but a text pane still cannot display it -- the claim would be asserted, not shown. The shareable repro is measure.py, committed in this directory, which recompiles the corpus and prints bytes/deflated/ratio; manual-case-compression.txt is its verified output.

**[#2792](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2792) — Need to report error when use constant which has offset bigger than root constant size.**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

No DXC has ever checked a cbuffer's size against its root constant block's num32BitConstants. RootConstants(b0, num32BitConstants = 1) with a two-float cbuffer at b0 compiles clean, exit 0, no diagnostic, and codegens the out-of-bounds read (extractvalue %dx.types.CBufRet.f32 %2, 1). Setting num32BitConstants = 2, making the shader correct, produces byte-identical output and the same shader hash: the field is parsed, serialised and printed but read by no validator, and DxilRootSignatureValidator registers a root constant as a one-register CBV range without passing Num32BitValues at all. Adjacent checking does run (binding b1 against a b0 cbuffer is rejected with 'Shader CBV descriptor range ... is not fully bound in root signature'), so this is a gap in that check rather than its absence. That check, VerifyRootSignatureWithShaderPSV, works from PSV bind info which carries no size, so a container-validation fix needs a PSV format change while a front-end fix does not. hlsl_clang_trunk does not diagnose it either, but also accepts the b1/b0 mismatch, so it has no root-signature-vs-shader checking yet at all. A request for a diagnostic that has never existed, not a regression.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`, `enhancement`, `check-in-clang`; remove `bug`.

**[#3189](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3189) — [SPIR-V] Descriptor bindings assigned before dead code elimination**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Reproduces exactly as filed on ground truth and on all 19 probeable releases (v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607); v1.4.1907 is invalid-probe (no SPIR-V codegen, confirmed by a flag-free control, since the primary capture was demoted only for an unknown flag). With the reporter reconstructed shift flags the used cbuffer c is decorated Binding 2 while the two unused cbuffers are fully DCE-eliminated; with no shift flags it is Binding 4, so the behaviour is not shift-specific. Source confirms decorateResourceBindings runs at SpirvEmitter.cpp:840, before spirv-opt at 972/988, and -O0 shows a=0 b=1 c=2 unchanged. DXIL mode compacts (c at cb0), as noted in the thread. Not a defect to fix: s-perron stated the design position in 2024 (default must not change; opt-in spirv-opt renumbering pass welcome), and DXC already ships -fspv-preserve-bindings which keeps unused resources rather than compacting them. Remaining actions are relabelling as an enhancement and two docs gaps in SPIR-V.rst: the behaviour itself, and -fspv-preserve-bindings, which is undocumented.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `up-for-grabs`, `docs`.

<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, ab5400907) and on every release back to the v1.4.1907 floor: a switch over an enum class covering every enumerator with no default:, in a non-void function, lowers the fall-off-the-end path to an LLVM 'unreachable', which DXIL disallows, so validation fails with 'Instructions must be of an allowed type' (E_FAIL, not a crash). Signing is not implicated: validation fails, so nothing is signed, and the reporter's 'DXIL.dll not found' warning is environmental -- every release probed had a dxil.dll beside it, and current builds do not consult one. Two secondary body claims have gone stale (see text-stale). Maintainers' 2024 position is won't-fix-in-DXC / handled in Clang; clang trunk emits no unreachable for a cut-down form of the same construct.

**[#8527](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8527) — pragma once is case sensitive**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.15422, eff900d54) and on every release v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607; not a regression. Title understates it: not case folding -- #pragma once is keyed on the path AS SPELLED, so './x.hlsli' vs 'x.hlsli' fails identically with the case held constant. DxcArgsFileSystemImpl::TryFindOrOpen matches includes by wcscmp on the spelled name and GetFileInformationByHandle reports the slot handle as the file index, so FileManager's UniqueID dedup sees two files. Matching-case control compiles clean; #ifndef guards are an effective workaround. Measured on Windows/NTFS only. No CE link: multi-file repro, and the single-file fold measures clang's pragma-once-in-main-file rule instead.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title says 'case sensitive'. Case is not the mechanism: #pragma once keys on the path as spelled, so './x' vs '././x' fails with case held constant. The real scope is wider than the title.

*Labels:* add `usability`, `check-in-clang`; remove `needs-triage`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* no valid single-file demonstration exists. The repro needs a header plus two includers and CE is single-file; CE also runs Linux, where the reported case-mismatched name does not exist. The obvious fold -- a file including itself under a different spelling of its own path -- was built, run on CE and REJECTED: the identical construction with a matching spelling fails the same way, so it measures clang's documented 'pragma once is ignored in the main file' rule, not this defect. Evidence: manual-case-godbolt.txt, variant-selfinclude-samespelling-main-debug.txt.

**[#8725](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8725) — [SER] Passing a payload by value to HitObject::Invoke asserts in CodeGen**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Confirmed on main (1.9.0.5433, ab5400907) and on all 5 releases that can compile lib_6_9. Passing a payload to dx::HitObject::Invoke through an in (by-value) parameter asserts at CGCall.cpp:2962 (reference binding to unmaterialized r-value), then emits 'bitcast %struct.Payload %v to %struct.Payload*' which release builds turn into a DXIL validation failure. Cause: AddHLSLIntrinsicMethod (SemaHLSL.cpp:6334-6340) makes every inout parameter of an object-method intrinsic an lvalue reference, with no record-type guard, unlike AddHLSLIntrinsicFunction (SemaHLSL.cpp:2123-2135); combined with the copy-in/copy-out temporary from EmitHLSLOutParamConversionInit the CGCall invariant breaks. Scope is wider than the title: dx::HitObject::TraceRay fails identically and a mutable static payload fails with no by-value parameter at all. Never worked; 15 older releases cannot express lib_6_9.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title scopes this to 'passing a payload by value to HitObject::Invoke'. Measured: dx::HitObject::TraceRay fails identically, and a mutable static payload passed straight to Invoke fails with no by-value parameter and no user function at all. So the title's 'by value' is one instance of a wider trigger -- an object-method intrinsic with an inout record parameter called with an argument whose address is not provably non-aliasing -- stated as a lead; only Invoke and TraceRay were measured.

*Labels:* add `crash`, `incorrect-code`, `diagnostic`, `sm6.9`; remove `needs-triage`.

**[#2202](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2202) — Validation error "DXIL intrinsic overload must be valid"**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Repros on main (eff900d5) and every release v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607. Must be compiled -HV 2018: at today's default -HV 2021 the front end rejects the vector-condition '?:' before codegen, so the validator never runs and it falsely looks fixed. -Vd shows codegen, not the validator, is at fault: the compile succeeds and emits 'call double @dx.op.dot3.f64', but hctdb declares Dot3 with overloads 'hf' (half/float only), so the validator is correct and -Vd just yields DXIL no runtime accepts. Literal-float ternary resolves to double; HLSL declares dot over 'numeric' (includes double), DXIL cannot express it. FXC compiles the same source in float. The reporter's second ask (no line number) was fixed in v1.6.2104. Same DXIL-level gap as open #8208 (mul on double4 -> dot4.f64).

*Labels:* add `type-system`, `fxc-disagrees`, `diagnostic`.

**[#2528](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2528) — Remainder of inout signature element not passed through when one component is modified**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main and on all 20 releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607. Writing one component of an inout signature element suppresses the pass-through of the rest: DXC emits only storeOutput(i32 5, i32 0, i32 0, i8 3, ...), no loadInput at all, and the output signature reads Used=w instead of xyzw. On SV_Position the DXIL validator catches it and the compile fails; on an ordinary varying (struct with TEXCOORD0) DXC exits 0 and silently emits a shader whose .yzw are undefined -- the impact evidence the 2024 dormancy note was missing. FXC passes all components through on the byte-identical sources.

*Labels:* add `correctness`, `check-in-clang`.

**[#2530](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2530) — Array bound with static const variable**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-sonnet-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Both cases in the body still fail on main (ab5400907). Case 1 fails on all 20 releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (linear scan); case 2 fails at both endpoints. FXC 10.1 compiles both. The bound is not an integer constant expression under the C++03 ICE rules DXC inherited from clang: CheckICE accepts an explicit cast only when its operand is a FloatingLiteral, so uint(<static const float>) is non-ICE, BuildArrayType makes a VariableArrayType and SemaType.cpp:2143 emits err_hlsl_vla. Case 2 is the same rule one level out via checkInitIsICE. float array[uint(1.0f)] and a static const uint bound both compile; dropping the cast instead gives err_array_size_non_int, a different path. clang's HLSL front end rejects both too, naming the constant-expression rule. Resolution is a language decision.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`.

**[#2673](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2673) — User command line defines are duplicated in debug info and in preprocessor**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.6)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Command-line -D defines are still duplicated: !dx.source.defines lists each define twice, exactly the node filed in 2020, on main (ab5400907) and on all 20 releases from v1.4.1907 to v1.9.2607. !dx.source.args shows the -D pair appended a second time, so the duplication happens in the argument list before the preprocessor or debug info see it. Corroborated in source: dxc.cpp:881-885 passes the argv (which still holds the -D flags) and m_Opts.Defines to IDxcCompiler::Compile, and BuildArguments re-appends one -D per define (dxclibrary.cpp:506-508) -- the de-duplication that already exists for -E/-T three lines above was never extended to defines. The reported configuration dependence still holds: the TAEF harness that runs the cited test passes nullptr,0 for defines (FileCheckerTest.cpp:573-575), so the test never exercises the driver path. DXIL is unaffected; the wrong data reaches IDxcPdbUtils and the PIX/DIA surfaces.

*Labels:* add `bug`, `debug info`.

**[#2923](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2923) — Structs passed to subroutines (can) cause the numbering pass to get confused about offsets of members**  
<sub>batch 008 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, SKILL.md step 10, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Still repros on main (1.9.0.5433, ab5400907): passing an amplification payload struct by value to a subroutine that calls DispatchMesh leaves main's own local mapped to six PIX virtual registers that are never written, with the six member writes numbered onto the inlined callee copy instead (both -Od and -O1); regressed in v1.6.2106 and numbered correctly in every earlier probeable release, so this agent-built repro may not be the reporter's 2020 instance.

*Labels:* add `PIX`, `bug`, `debug info`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* Compiler Explorer can only run dxc. The symptom is in metadata written by the PIX passes (-dxil-dbg-value-to-dbg-declare, -dxil-annotate-with-virtual-regs), which live in dxcompiler.dll and are driven by dxopt, not by dxc; CE has no way to run them and no way to show ILDB metadata. repro.hlsl itself compiles cleanly (exit 0, no diagnostics) on every release tested, so a CE link would show a clean compile and nothing about the defect. The runnable repro is run-2923.cmd in this directory.

**[#3259](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3259) — Crash in TranslatePtrIfUsedByLoweredFn**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Still crashes on Debug main (ab5400907): DXASSERT_NOMSG(Ty) at lib/DXIL/DxilUtil.cpp:877 in hlsl::dxilutil::WrapInArrayTypes, called from TranslatePtrIfUsedByLoweredFn (the frame in the title), exit 0x80000003. Root cause is unchanged from the reporter's 2020 diagnosis: GetLoweredUDT returns nullptr for a struct with an embedded object type (HLLowerUDT.cpp:67, and :72 for nested structs), ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:426 does not check it, so the null reaches WrapInArrayTypes at :436. Not Debug-only: DXASSERT_NOMSG is a no-op under NDEBUG (Global.h:369) and the null type flows on to Builder.CreateAlloca at :450, so all 19 releases that support as_6_5 (v1.5.2010, released three weeks before this was filed, through v1.9.2607) access-violate reading address 0. v1.5.2010 crashes with empty stderr. Compiler Explorer's dxc_1_6_2112 and dxc_trunk both SIGSEGV. Any HLSL object type triggers it (SamplerState too) at any nesting depth; a uint payload compiles cleanly. Confined to DispatchMesh's payload operand -- IsPtrUsedByLoweredFn (ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:310) has TraceRay/ReportHit/CallShader commented out under a TODO.

*Labels:* add `incorrect-code`.

**[#3693](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3693) — Vector element index out-of-bounds not leading to compile error**  
<sub>batch 008 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, SKILL.md step 10, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Still reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, ab5400907) and on every release back to v1.6.2104: DXC has the "vector element index out of bounds" error but never reaches it when the subscript is the index operand of another subscript, so the element becomes undef and is used as a buffer index. FXC has no raytracing profile, so the cross-compiler comparison used a compute restating of the same construct; FXC rejects that with X3504, while clang-dxc trunk misses this form and also the plain form DXC catches. Arrays have the identical hole (g_vertices[a[3]] silent, uint x = a[3] diagnosed).

*Labels:* add `fxc-disagrees`, `incorrect-code`.

**[#8737](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8737) — Atomics on RWTexture2DMS result in silent UB or ICE**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Both reported symptoms confirmed on main (eff900d54) and on every SM 6.7-capable release since v1.7.2207. ICE: InterlockedMax(tex.sample[s][uv],..) exits E_FAIL with 'llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!' (a thrown hlsl::Exception, identical in Debug and Release); also fires with a constant sample index, other atomics and RWTexture2DMSArray. Silent case: compiles with exit 0 and no diagnostic, emitting dx.op.atomicBinOp with 'i32 undef' in the last coordinate on a 2dMS UAV -- byte-identical to the same atomic on a plain RWTexture2D. DXIL.rst:1876-1887 does not list Texture2DMS among AtomicBinOp's valid resource types and gen_intrin_main.txt declares no interlocked method on RWTexture2DMS, so this is invalid input DXC fails to diagnose, not valid input it miscompiles. The validator does not catch it either (DxilValidation.cpp:2412 checks UAV-ness, not resource kind).

*Labels:* add `crash`, `incorrect-code`, `diagnostic`, `sm6.7`; remove `needs-triage`.

**[#3251](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3251) — Missing implementation for HLOpcodeGroup::NotHL in TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `ab5400907` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Still asserts on Debug main (ab5400907): DXASSERT(0, 'not implemented yet') at lib/HLSL/HLOperationLower.cpp:8801 in TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy, exit 0x80000003. Reported mechanism is unchanged -- 'p.lhSampleData = g_lhSampleData' becomes one llvm.memcpy out of the legacy cbuffer, whose HLOpcodeGroup is NotHL, and the cbuffer-user walker has no case for it. Only the line moved: 6207 was the CallInst arm's final else; PR #3034 (eaa7f95d0, 6 days after filing) inserted an IntrinsicInst branch, so memcpy now hits its inner else at 8801 (outer one is 8804, identical text). Reached from DxilGenerationPass::GenerateDxilOperations -> TranslateHLSubscript(CBufferSubscript) -> TranslateCBOperationsLegacy. Not $Globals-specific (an explicit cbuffer block traps too) and not payload-agnostic (the same copy into an RWStructuredBuffer in cs_6_0 compiles clean) -- the DispatchMesh payload is what keeps the copy a memcpy into DXIL lowering. Field-by-field copy compiles clean on main and back to v1.5.2010, and is a workaround. All 19 probeable releases fail, in 4 different shapes: access violation 0xC0000005 (9, one of them with completely empty output), DXC_E_LLVM_UNREACHABLE 0x80AA001C DataLayout::getTypeSizeInBits (2), E_FAIL 0x80004005 with UNREACHABLE executed (7), E_FAIL with llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type (1) -- so 8 of 19 exit with the same status as a syntax error and a message-keyed predicate would have reported this as fixed.


## Provenance and limits

- Ground truth is a **Debug** build of `main` (3 commits across batches). Debug matters: many older issues are asserts, which a Release build compiles out.
- **The release bisection floor is v1.4.1907** (2019-07), the oldest release shipping a usable `dxc`. For issues filed before it, "always reproduced" means "for as long as it is possible to check". SPIR-V issues have a higher floor still.
- **Compiler Explorer runs Release builds**, so a Debug-only assert looks clean there. CE corroborates the local build; it never overrules it. `dxc_trunk` is a rolling build and is not reproducible over time.
- **Sampling is deliberately unrepresentative.** Batches over-weight the oldest issues, so the verdict distribution here does not generalise to the backlog.

Per-batch reports, including the method findings that changed how later batches were run: [batch 001](batch-001.md), [batch 002](batch-002.md), [batch 003](batch-003.md), [batch 004](batch-004.md), [batch 005](batch-005.md), [batch 006](batch-006.md), [batch 007](batch-007.md), [batch 008](batch-008.md).
